name: Senegalia

project_scope.selection_mode: Master Plant Pool field-ID comparison; not automatically a canonical species install
project_scope.native_range_status: TEXAS STATE native for all three (POWO), strict target-zone counties unassessed.
project_scope.primary_local_anchor: Senegalia roemeriana — Hays flora confirms wild local occurrence
project_scope.current_status: Exactly one source-pool species installed with verified-license photo; other proposed comparisons not installed.

look_here_first: FEEL FOR THE TINY BACKWARD-CURVED PRICKLES along stems (CAREFULLY). Determine the flower cluster SHAPE: round creamy WHITE heads → S. roemeriana; elongated pale spikes → investigate S. greggii/S. wrightii. Then count leaflets, inspect the stalk and mature flat pod.

shared_traits: Woody shrubs or small trees with alternate bipinnate leaves.
Hooks or recurved PRICKLES often on stems between nodes, unlike paired straight STIPULAR SPINES of Vachellia.
Many small pale flowers collected into a globose head or an elongate spike depending on species.
Flattened pods; seed count, margin, width and constrictions matter for species IDs.
priority: Armature: recurved prickles along internode vs straight paired nodal spines
ROUND head vs ELONGATE spike before counting pinnae
Leaflet length and pair counts (overlap; only supportive)
Flower-head/stalk and bud vs open flower macro
Compare mature flat pods and their margins on same scale
study_strategy.warning: All three have been historically called Acacia or catclaw. Do not force a species from a nonflowering twig; leaflets/prickles overlap. S. wrightii was once treated as Acacia greggii var. wrightii, but Kew now accepts species S. wrightii. S. roemeriana is an important Hays County ID.

quick_key.if: round cream/white flower HEADS, hooked prickle; Hill Country
quick_key.then: Senegalia roemeriana — roundflower catclaw (local high priority)

quick_key.if: elongate cream-colored flower SPIKES, catclaw prickles, numerous very tiny leaflets
elongate cream flower SPIKES, catclaw, noticeably larger leaflets (~3–6 mm) and often 1–4 pinna pairs
quick_key.then: Senegalia wrightii — Wright acacia (confirm reproductive structures)

quick_key.if: bright yellow spherical heads AND paired straight nodal stipular spines
